The resulting band structure is quite exotic; fermions in the third band have an unusual rounded picture-frame Fermi surface (essentially two concentric squircles), leading to imperfect nesting. We develop a generalized SO(3, 1) × SO(3, 1) theory describing the spin and charge degrees of freedom simultaneously, and show that the system can develop a coupled spin-charge-density wave order. This ordering is absent in studies of the Hubbard model that treat spin and charge density separately. 我们推导并讨论了一个实验上可行的模型，描述了在光晶格中包含一个公度但交错的塞曼场的超冷原子。由此产生的能带结构相当奇特；第三能带中的费米子具有一个不寻常的圆角画框形状的费米面（本质上是两个同心的方圆形），导致不完全的嵌套。我们发展了一个广义的 SO(3, 1) × SO(3, 1) 理论，同时描述了自旋和电荷自由度，并表明该系统可以产生耦合的自旋-电荷密度波序。这种有序态在将自旋和电荷密度分开处理的哈伯德模型研究中是不存在的。 **optical lattice**: 光晶格，由多束激光干涉形成的周期性势阱，用于囚禁超冷原子。 **Zeeman field**: 塞曼场，由磁场引起的原子能级分裂，等效于一个有效磁场。 **Fermi surface**: 费米面，在动量空间中，被电子占据的态与未被占据的态之间的边界。 **imperfect nesting**: 不完全嵌套，费米面的一部分平移一定波矢后与另一部分近似重合，但存在偏差，导致弱的不稳定性。 **Hubbard model**: 哈伯德模型，描述晶格中电子相互作用的最简模型，包含动能项和格点库仑排斥项。 > > 术语 "SO(3,1)×SO(3,1)" 可解释，但可能不是首次出现的核心术语？我们可以在后面解释。这里可以添加解释，但摘要中已经有很多术语。我们选择性地添加最核心的。 > > 接下来是 Introduction 标题： > > ## Introduction > > 引言 > > 接下来是 Introduction 下的段落。我们需要根据输入文本拆分。输入文本从 "Introduction" 后，紧接着 "Ultracold atoms in optical lattices have recently emerged ..." 这段。然后有 "We derive a lattice model, equally applicable ..." 一段。然后 "For particles with two spin states, ..." 一段。然后 "To account for interactions, ..." 一段。然后 "Imperfect nesting along the diagonal ..." 一段。然后 "At the interac" 然后图1代码块，然后 arXiv 行，然后 "2" 行，然后 "confining motion to the xˆ − yˆ plane." 开始的新段落。我们需要把这些碎片整理成连贯的单元。但按照任务，我们遵循输入顺序。我们按原文顺序输出。 > > 仔细看输入文本中 Introduction 部分： > > 
Introduction Ultracold atoms in optical lattices have recently emerged as a class of condensed matter systems, where the properties of the many-body Hamiltonian are under exquisite experimental control. Interfering laser beams in one, two or three dimensions (D) create standing waves: nearly perfect optical lattices for atoms with lattice spacing and topology set by the laser geometry and wavelength [1]. Optical lattices not only allow for the implementation of different lattice models without defects, but also open a wide range of possibilities to manipulate the parameters of the model describing ultracold bosons, fermions, or mixtures thereof. For example, the hopping parameters, local chemical potential, and often even the interaction strength can be tuned at will. Most optical lattice experiments use atoms in a single state [2], however, some experiments study mixtures of atoms in two or more atomic “spin” states, each of which can experience different lattice potentials [3–5]. We derive a lattice model, equally applicable to bosons and fermions, with an effective Zeeman magnetic field including a term alternating in sign on a site-by-site basis [6]. In condensed matter systems, the Zeeman field couples strongly to electrons near the Fermi surface [7], and in more orchidaceous situations, it breaks local timereversal invariance in topological insulators [8, 9]. For particles with two spin states, our lattice model has four low-energy bands, and the third is shaped as a squarish, deformed, Mexican hat for a wide range of system parameters. By filling the system with fermions, we obtain a peculiar Fermi surface, consisting of the boundaries of a squarish ring, essentially two concentric squircles [10]. The particular shape of the Fermi surface suggests that nesting effects should be expected. To account for interactions, we develop an SO(3, 1) × SO(3, 1) description of the charge and spin degrees of freedom. Imperfect nesting along the diagonal connecting corners of the Fermisurface gives rise to a coupled spin-charge-density wave (SCDW) instability at a critical interaction strength Uc. We calculate the imaginary part of the trace of the random phase approximation (RPA) susceptibility to study the collective excitations of the system. At the interac
